symptoms: Sunken, circular to oval lesions with black concentric rings of fungal acervuli on ripe fruits; tips of branches wither, dry and turn ash grey downwards (dieback).
management: Consult local agricultural university / KVK package of practices for registered treatment.
prevention: Practice crop rotation, field hygiene, and use certified seeds.

diseases.scientific_name: Chilli leaf curl virus (ChiLCV) & Thrips/Mite complex
symptoms: Upward curling and canoeing of leaves (thrips/virus) or downward cupping with inverted boat shape (yellow mite); leaves turn leathery, brittle and crinkled.
management: Consult local agricultural university / KVK package of practices for registered treatment.
prevention: Practice crop rotation, field hygiene, and use certified seeds.

symptoms: Characteristic visual lesions, discoloration or foliar distress associated with Anthracnose.
management: Isolate affected foliage, apply approved bio-fungicide or targeted treatment.
prevention: Implement crop rotation, avoid water stagnation, and sanitize farm implements regularly.

symptoms: Leaves curl upwards (boat-shaped); crinkling of foliage with bronze coloration on undersurface; vector of Chilli Leaf Curl Virus.
management: Spray Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.8ml/L or Fipronil 5% SC @ 1.5ml/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.25g/L.

symptoms: Leaves curl downwards (inverted boat); elongation of petiole (rat-tail symptom); leaves turn deep green and brittle.
management: Spray Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1ml/L or Wettable Sulphur 80% WP @ 3g/L or Abamectin 1.9% EC @ 0.75ml/L.

correction: Foliar spray of Magnesium Sulphate @ 5g/L or 10g/L at 15-day intervals.

healthy_signs: Turgid, deep green leaves with crisp texture and no chlorosis
Vigorous flowering and uniform fruit set free from blemishes or sunken spots
Clean root crown without fungal damping-off or collar decay
Absence of curling, puckering, or mosaic leaf mottling
management: Prune lower diseased foliage with sanitized secateurs; dispose of off-field
Apply targeted bio-fungicides (Bacillus subtilis / Trichoderma) or copper-based sprays
Control sucking insect vectors promptly using yellow sticky traps and botanical sprays
prevention: Adopt raised nursery beds with nylon insect netting to prevent early vector transmission
Mulch beds with silver-black reflective plastic mulch to deter thrips and aphids
Water using drip irrigation at the base to keep foliage completely dry
Regularly rogue out and safely destroy virus-infected or blighted plants
